newsitem.title: USA: Cargill says to shut canola crush plant at end-Oct.
newsitem.headline: Cargill says to shut canola crush plant at end-Oct.

text.p: Cargill Ltd said it was temporarily ceasing its canola crushing operations in its Clavet, Saskatchewan facility at the end of the month.
"Canadian canola crushing margins are extremely poor right now so we will remain closed until market conditions turn around," the company said in a statement.
The Cargill plant, recently built at a cost of C$53 million, was due to reach its full capacity of 2,000 tonnes a day this fall.
The company said it was going to continue accepting canola deliveries through its elevators to serve the export seed market.
"We believe that fundamentally there is a strong long term viability for the industry and we remain committed to the plant," the company said.
Cargill Ltd is the Canadian subisidiary of Minnesota-based Cargill Inc.
